summary: Burst traffic caused routing to shared-GPU pool that incurred prolonged warmup and long p99 latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Noteable Analytics reported a sudden spike in p95/p99 latency and several 504 timeouts during two short bursts of low-to-moderate QPS on 2026-03-10. Traffic that normally hits the customer's dedicated variant (d-ml-dedicated-1) was routed to a shared GPU pool variant (shared-gpu-s1) during the bursts, which incurred image pull and model shard reallocation delays and produced long warmup times.

Impact:
- Several requests returned 504s and many experienced p99 latency > 7s for ~90 seconds during each burst.
- Customer-facing application errors and degraded UX for the affected windows.
- No persistent data loss; requests that retried after warmup generally succeeded.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted prod in us-west region.
- Customer on dedicated plan with routing policy that permits overflow to shared pool when dedicated capacity is transiently saturated.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1. Generate a short burst of concurrent chat completions (10-30 reqs/s) for model redwood/titan-xl-v1 pinned to customer's dedicated variant.
2. Temporarily reduce available replicas for the dedicated variant (simulated via scaling event or temporary quota).
3. Observe routing decision: requests overflowed to shared-gpu-s1 variant.
4. Observe increased p50->p99 latency for first ~60-120s due to container image pull, model shard fetch, and KV cache miss warmup.

Logs & telemetry pointers:
- Router traces: /dash/router/trace?requestId=... (see linked_confluence_pages).
- Serving runtime logs show container pull durations ~25-40s and shard assembly times ~15-35s for affected replicas.
- KV cache miss rate spiked to 98% at the start of both bursts.
- Sample errors: 504 gateway-timeout where backend exceeded 60s.

Current status:
- SRE has captured packet of traces and start/end markers for both burst windows.
- Engineering is reproducing in staging with identical routing policy to validate mitigation options.

investigation_notes:
Hypotheses:
- Overflow policy allowed routing to shared pool variant that has larger image footprint and serialized shard assembly, causing >60s tail for some requests.
- Short burst pattern caused autoscaler to not pre-provision warm replicas; shared pool replicas had to cold-pull images and model shards.
- KV cache empty state on new replicas produced high initial token latencies.
Findings:
- Confirmed image pull and shard assembly timings from runtime logs.
- Router decision logic discussed: overflow triggers on transient dedicated saturation with no distinction for burst duration.
- Reproduced locally by simulating dedicated capacity drop; warmup pattern matches production traces.
resolution:
Workarounds applied:
1) Increased overflow threshold for the customer's routing policy to reduce chance of overflow on short bursts.
2) Enabled fast-fail preference for bursts under 30s so requests prefer wait-for-dedicated replica instead of overflowing immediately.
3) Runtime patch to reduce sidecar startup footprint and parallelize shard fetches has been merged and rolled out to canary.
Permanent follow-ups:
- Engineering to finish gradual rollout of runtime optimization to all shared-gpu pools in us-west by 2026-03-18.
- Product to add a routing policy toggle for 'avoid-shared-on-short-burst' exposed via Console for Dedicated customers.
- Add a proactive prewarm heuristic in autoscaler to detect short bursts and pre-warm replicas for pinned models.
Status: Mitigations in place and customer-verification scheduled. Close after 2026-03-18 rollout if canary metrics are stable.
